conventions: חָרַם hiphil is rendered 'utterly destroy(ed)' throughout the chapter (vv. 3, 8, 9, 15, 18, 20). No infinitive absolute stands in any of them, so 'utterly' is the verb's own rendering and the whole is one unit headed on destroy; the ASV margin 'devote(d)' is read and set aside under rule 38.

עֲמָלֵק is rendered by the ASV both as the bare name 'Amalek' (vv. 2, 3, 5, 20) and as the gentilic 'the Amalekites' (vv. 7, 18, 20, 32). Where the gentilic is written, the supplied 'the' joins the name's unit under rule 15, headed on Amalekites, exactly as it does on the true gentilic עֲמָלֵקִי (vv. 6, 15); where 'Amalek' is written the name takes only its own word and any 'of' the rectum's relation gives it.

שָׁמַע בְּקוֹל → 'obey(ed) the voice' / 'obeyed their voice' (vv. 19, 20, 22, 24): the ASV writes no word for the בְּ in this chapter and it is unrepresented under rule 40 every time. The second 'in' of v. 22 ('delight in burnt offerings ... as in obeying') is the distributed repetition of the earlier בְּ of בְּעֹלוֹת under rule 25, not a rendering of the בְּ of בְּקוֹל.

Toponyms carrying an article — הַכַּרְמֶלָה and הַגִּלְגָּל (v. 12), בַּגִּלְגָּל (vv. 21, 33), הָרָמָתָה (v. 34) — take no 'the' in the ASV, so the article is its own unrepresented unit under rule 29. A directive he standing on the name takes the written 'to' under rule 32 (Carmel v. 12, Ramah v. 34); where none stands, the supplied 'to' before the bare name is the name's under rule 33 (Gilgal v. 12, Gibeah v. 34).
report: Read all 35 verses end to end against the candidate table. Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by the ASV's own wording: waw takes whichever connective is written (And/but/So/Then/also/for/that/therefore/'And as'), לְ before a name is of/unto/Hath or unrepresented as the ASV renders it, לְ + מֶלֶךְ is 'to be' where the ASV writes it (vv. 1, 11) and unrepresented where it does not (v. 17), and the object marker is unrepresented in all 24 occurrences.

Constructions repeated across verses are analysed one way each: חָרַם → utterly destroy(ed) as one unit (vv. 3, 8, 9, 15, 18, 20); עֲמָלֵק → 'the Amalekites' with its supplied the on the name (vv. 7, 18, 20, 32) beside bare 'Amalek' (vv. 2, 3, 5, 20); שָׁמַע בְּקוֹל with the בְּ unrepresented (vv. 19, 20, 22, 24); article on toponyms unrepresented (vv. 12, 21, 33, 34); arthrous rectum counted by rule 29 (vv. 9, 14, 15, 21) and the one anarthrous rectum fronted (v. 32); 'Now therefore' split now/therefore (vv. 1, 25); purposive waw → that (vv. 25, 30); נָא → I pray thee (vv. 25, 30); substantival/attributive article → that / that which (vv. 9, 19, 28).

The six added units (v. 2 himself, v. 17 made, v. 22 and, v. 27 Saul, v. 30 yet, v. 35 came) are each licensed by no morpheme in their verse and are not folded elsewhere in another verse: v. 12's resumed 'he' rests on a Saul written earlier in that verse (rule 25), while v. 27's Saul is not written in that verse (rule 17). Two remain judgment calls already named in their notes rather than errors: v. 17 'made' could instead join רֹאשׁ as a becoming-copula under rule 20, and v. 18 'they' sits on the object suffix rather than the infinitive's subject suffix because the passive recasting makes the object the English subject.

BSB disagreements are all convention: object markers, prepositions the ASV recasts bare (rule 40), articles the ASV does not write, the apodosis waw of v. 27 (rule 14), the interrogative הַ of v. 22 whose fronted Hath is the possessive לְ's (rule 43), and the v. 18 suffix tie noted above. None is a genuine error and no edge was changed.

No contract promotion or amendment: nothing here generalises beyond rules the contract already states. Four chapter-wide judgments are recorded as conventions so a later verse pass need not rediscover them.
